judged.rule: The opening shows one recognizable behavior and asks one specific question about it that the episode answers within its scope.
The first meaningful causal answer is on screen by about 8–12 seconds, or the episode records why orientation needs longer; no part catalogue precedes it.
Each question gets a visible answer that motivates the next dependency, and parts are introduced at their functional use.
One marked physical event is readable at phone size, with its contact or transfer given enough frame area and competing cues reduced.
The final demonstration revisits the opening action or state and makes the hidden cause visible.
Every narrated causal interaction shows its input, its contact or transfer, and its response.
Every designed interaction event has a synchronized cue, shares an evolving cue, or has a recorded reason for silence.
No run of three or more shots repeats the same framing and operation with only labels changing.
The visible object or active subassembly is centred in x=80..1000, y=430..1410 at 80–95% of the stage, with at least 60 px clear above the caption.
Every view is layered 2.5D illustration: no standalone flat 2D diagram scene, true 3D scene or mixed medium.

sources.duration_seconds: frame.md productionDefaults (90 seconds within one output frame); DIRECTION.md#version-2-production-defaults
sources.motion.max_static_seconds: DIRECTION.md#version-4-visual-lock-interaction-and-sound (roughly five seconds without a state change triggers review)
sources.captions.region: frame.md components.caption (left 108, top 1500, width 848, two lines of 46 px/1.3 with 18 px padding)
sources.audio: frame.md frontmatter audio (interaction SFX required; music optional)
